{"notes": "VISIT 4 (left 6:15). I don't know who placed which domino. I did not see the push or the result, so I can't judge how it went.

TABLE: The fish outline is complete and connected from START, with both tail tips reached. The 3 pale, disconnected dominoes near (23-24, 8.3-9) were never fixed or removed. The team finished without dealing with them, and the open question is still unanswered: nobody took responsibility for them. They could disrupt the chain at the crossing. Check after the push whether they mattered.

SOFIA: Strong concept, plan and split of work earlier. At 5:45 she was calm and ready. Her 2:30 tail inspection either didn't happen or missed the strays beside her own section. Ask her. Execution is good overall, with a quality-control gap. Direction and communication are still her strengths.

OMAR: Clean handoff earlier. He offered at 2:30 to fix an off-side domino, but the strays remain, and he said nothing at 5:45. Ownership intent is not backed by follow-through I can verify. Ask whether those were the dominoes he meant.

HANA: First words I've heard from her: a short 'hands off, here we go' at 5:45. The belly she built is connected and clean, so her output is solid. I still don't know why she is so quiet. Ask her directly about blockers and about her role.

JACK: Positive, team-minded closer. He credited the team and called hands-off at 5:45. He took on tilt and gap checking but I never saw him do it, and the strays survived. Ask what he checked. His collaboration looks good, but his execution evidence is thin.

REVIEW QUESTIONS: Who saw the strays? Why were they left? Who actually did the checking?"}
